lead: Port St. Lucie is one of Florida's newest big cities, and most homes are owner-occupied. Hurricanes, tornadoes and aging roofs on early-2000s homes drive its water damage.
risk: hurricane and tornado damage, aging roofs and heavy rain
why: The median Port St. Lucie home was built in 2002, and 84% are owner-occupied. Many of those homes now have roofs that are 20 years old or more, the age when Florida insurers start asking for a replacement. Shingles that look fine from the ground can lift in high wind. Once a storm opens the roof, rain soaks insulation and drywall quickly.

Hurricanes bring more than wind. In October 2024, Hurricane Milton spun up tornadoes across St. Lucie County. One struck the Spanish Lakes area near Fort Pierce and killed several people. Heavy rain also fills the city's canal system, and low streets can flood when storms stall. Summer humidity means wet drywall and carpet can grow mold within a day or two.
image_alt: Street covered in storm debris and damaged structures
image_caption: Hurricane winds leave debris and open roofs across Port St. Lucie neighborhoods.
problems: Early-2000s homes in Torino, St. Lucie West
Homes with roofs near 20 years old
tips: Know your roof's age; insurers often check at 15 to 20 years.
Add hurricane straps or a wind mitigation upgrade for a lower premium.
Buy flood insurance early; it usually takes 30 days to start.
Run AC or dehumidifiers after any leak to stop mold.
areas: Calls come from Tradition, St. Lucie West, Torino, Sandpiper Bay, Riverland and Southbend Lakes, plus Fort Pierce, Jensen Beach and Stuart.

faq.q: Will my Port St. Lucie insurer cover an old roof?
faq.a: Many Florida insurers limit coverage on roofs older than 15 to 20 years, or pay only part of the cost. Some will not write a new policy until the roof is replaced. Check your policy for a roof payment schedule. A wind mitigation report can also lower your premium.
